ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, at a height h above the ground there are two small balls A and B. A is projected horizontally with initial velocity v0, while at the same time B slides down along a smooth inclined plane with an inclination angle of 45° with an initial velocity v0 of the same magnitude. If A and B reach the ground at the same time, find the magnitude of the initial velocity v0.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a vertical support, and the height from the top end to the horizontal ground is marked as h; at the top end, two small balls A and B are marked. A is projected from the top end to the left with horizontal initial velocity v0, and the figure uses a dashed line to represent its projectile trajectory. B moves downward from the same top end along the smooth inclined plane on the right side; the angle between the inclined plane and the ground is marked as 45°, and the magnitude of B's initial velocity is also marked as v0, with the direction downward along the inclined plane. Then reason: A undergoes horizontal projectile motion, the initial velocity in the vertical direction is 0, and the falling height is h, so the common motion time t satisfies h=\frac12gt^2, giving t=\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}. B slides down along the 45° smooth inclined plane, the length of the inclined plane is s=\frac{h}{\sin45^\circ}=\sqrt2h, and the acceleration along the inclined plane is a=g\sin45^\circ=\frac{g}{\sqrt2}. The displacement equation of B along the inclined plane is \sqrt2h=v_0t+\frac12\cdot\frac{g}{\sqrt2}t^2. Substituting t=\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}, there is \sqrt2h=v_0\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}+\frac{h}{\sqrt2}, so v_0\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}=\frac{h}{\sqrt2}, and solving gives v_0=\frac{\sqrt{gh}}{2}.
